note: One task instance, one artifact. The five shipped files are the fts-appeal-003 worker artifact ac529cd4e9d4da90f804ecef425e74c94a946b857fe39095fd73a0407506b8c0 (gate 1.5.0 on the full artifact, failed_checks empty, exact-byte --accept on the worker; re-accepted from the fetched bytes inside baseline job fts-baseline-002 before any score existed). The package's code/ carries the construction script, the references implementation, the worker run order, the runner-workdir materializer and the gate; baseline/ the runner-contract baseline. The holdout ships as an asset like the other splits; it is not copied into any runner workdir and was never evaluated. The prediction instant is the appeal's public launch (requirements first published; event_time), months before the plan year closes. The 2026.10-era prior-outcome features that allowed exact cross-row label recovery (the 2026-11-01 queue audit's P0) were removed in the fts-appeal-003 rebuild: no shipped column reads any row's outcome, and the only history-derived column (years_since_country_prior) reads strictly-earlier appeal YEARS, never labels. Recorded finding carried in measurements.json, RELEASE_NOTES.md and VERIFICATION.md: on the identical 139 eval rows the stock runner's full model scores 0.6452 while the persistence reference (scorer-side recompute of the last prior same-country coverage from prior-in-time labels, train+eval only) scores 0.7171136653895275 - the model trails persistence by 0.0719 and every measured simple reference except the majority-class rate, recorded as no demonstrated headroom under this protocol for the stock runner, with the information-asymmetry note (the model is deliberately denied the last prior outcome under the operator's P0 standard while the persistence reference reads it scorer-side) beside every quoted figure; a solver must beat persistence_last_coverage for any headroom claim. Labeled eval is development/validation; holdout is final scoring and stays sealed until the design is frozen.
